requirement: SPEC.md section 4, and the compatibility contract above
note: A file, from the JSON on disk to the objects a document holds, and the replay that reads its journal back. A load goes through the mutation channel, so the refusals here run past the shape of the file into the integrity checks and the cycle check, and a document that decodes cleanly can still be refused for what it means. A derived value never reaches a file, so the cases carrying a rect ask both engines to build nine derived slots that the JSON never held, and read the arithmetic back. The slots of an answer are a list rather than an object, so their order is part of what is compared: the case that lists "area" before the slots the schema declares after it would catch a load that rebuilt the map in schema order instead of the order the file wrote. A round trip answers with the document that comes back from its own saved text rather than with the text, because the spelling JSON gives a number belongs to the JSON writer of each language. The two writers agree on every number a document can hold, which the unit tests beside each engine pin, and this fixture asks the question a file actually raises: whether the other engine reads it back to the same document. A loaded journal is deliberately permissive, so the entries travel as the JSON they arrived as and each one is read only when a replay reaches it. The malformed entries here are refused in written sentences rather than by whatever the runtime throws, which is what D-006 and D-007 in docs/RUST_PORT.md settle. Two cases a file can carry are missing from this fixture on purpose, both recorded under D-007. An object whose type names no schema loads in TypeScript and is refused in Rust, and a literal past the range of a binary64 is read as infinity by one JSON parser and refused by the other. Each engine's own tests carry those.
